statement: Under RH, if b(Y)→0, a(Y)/b(Y)→r in (0,1), and a(Y)logY→infinity, the cosine prime band Y^a<p≤Y^b, centered by sum 1/p or its actual mean, converges in law and every fixed moment to N(0,(1/2)log(1/r)).
hypotheses: Symmetric strict derivative-square tail. Uses bounded aggregate polynomial powers at each fixed degree and the reconstructed sharp interface. Effective parameter estimates require effective cutoff moduli and the audited effective exceptional-prime estimate. This record alone is scalar.

statement: For any fixed 0<a<b<infinity, globally derivative-square tilted rooted CUE Fourier bands converge jointly in law and every fixed moment to the one-root-reinserted rank-two-removed sine-projection linear statistics. The centered statistic is defined in L2 and has the regularized determinant in the director note.
hypotheses: Global Haar-matrix/root-label tilt, not per-matrix root normalization. Positive lower frequency, a fixed finite family, and centered L2 or symmetric summation. Absolute point sums diverge for the nontrivial individual cosine band. The quadratic trace correction in det2 is required. No RH or arithmetic law transfer.

statement: For every fixed integer r≥0 with rb<1/2, the raw rth moment of the RH derivative-weighted cosine band converges to r! times [z^r] exp(H z+H z²/4)[(1−d z)^4+q z(1−d z)], where H=log(b/a), d=b−a and q=2(b³−a³)/3.
hypotheses: One fixed 0<a<b and the exact symmetric strict tail. Each degree r uses aggregate arms through Y^(rb) and fixed declared exponent below 1/2. Only the source-admissible finite coefficient window is evaluated; growing r or all orders at fixed b are not justified.

statement: For every fixed 0<a<b, the formal all-order coefficient sequence of exp(H z+H z²/4)[(1−d z)^4+q z(1−d z)] cannot be the moments of a positive probability. Its entire formal MGF vanishes at 1/d; Gaussian-polynomial even-moment domination makes this a rigorous contradiction. A degree-70 negative Gram witness at [1/20,1/10] is independently interval-verified.
hypotheses: Pure unconditional statement about the formal sequence, not about source validity or actual higher arithmetic moments. The witness uses formal orders through 140, while that arithmetic band supplies only orders 0–4. All genuine source-window Hankel tests remain positive.

statement: Under RH, for every prime subset I of (Y^(r0 b),Y^b], h=sum_I 1/p, one has E_Y|sum_I(cos(gamma logp)/sqrt p−1/p)|^4≤C_M min(h²+(logY)^−M,(logY)²h²), hence ≤C h^(3/2) for M≥6.
hypotheses: Fixed 0<r0<1, b→0 and b logY→infinity, same symmetric strict derivative-square tail, all subsets uniformly at sufficiently large Y. The exact local-mass bound uses analytic disks for zeta D_I² and the classical continuous fourth moment. A full-range Ch² bound is not asserted.

statement: Under RH, X_Y(r)=sum_(Y^(r0 b)<p≤Y^(r b))[cos(gamma logp)/sqrt p−1/p] converges in D([r0,1]), J1, to B_((1/2)log(r/r0)).
hypotheses: Fixed 0<r0<1, b(Y)→0, b(Y)logY→infinity and the symmetric strict derivative-square tail. Uses the two-scale fourth lemma, exact reciprocal-clock interpolation, vanishing jumps, and fixed-dimensional Gaussian projections. In-principle effective onset needs computable r0, effective cutoff moduli and the audited effective aggregate input; no numerical onset.

statement: Under RH, for bounded real Riemann-integrable cosine/sine weights supported in [a,b] with 0<a<b<1/6, the centered third tensor matches globally derivative-square rooted CUE. The CSS entry is 12 integral f(x)(x²−2)dx integral g(y)y dy integral h(z)z dz. Odd-sine entries vanish. Same-band CSS is (Delta3−6Delta1)Delta2².
hypotheses: Signed primary HLZ extraction, aggregate length Y^(3b), repeated-prime cancellation, exact strict tail, and one deterministic root on the CUE side. Fourth moments are uniformly bounded. This adds the mixed tensor to the prior pure cosine cubic, not a full arithmetic law. At [1/20,1/10] CSS=−21537/1280000000.

statement: For nonnegative bounded Riemann-integrable cosine and sine weights with positive integrals, supported in a common [a,b]⊂(0,1/6), any arithmetic weak subsequential vector limit has dependent cosine/sine coordinates despite exact zero covariance. The supports may be disjoint.
hypotheses: Assumes RH and the same strict tail. Uniform fourth moments transfer the nonzero centered CSS entry; independence would force it to vanish. Pointwise nonzero weights confined to null sets are excluded. Existence or uniqueness of a full vector limit and Gaussianity of the sine marginal are not asserted.
